channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India: Russian dependence and security focus – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Anubhuti Sahay and Saurav Anand highlight India’s rapidly rising reliance on Russian Oil, now at 44% of crude imports since the Middle East crisis, up from 2% in 2021.

item.title: Gold falls as strong US PMI data gives Fed room to raise rates again
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Wednesday as expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes lift the US Dollar (USD) and weigh on the non-yielding metal. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,285 during American trading hours, down 1.60% on the day.

item.title: Breaking: US S&P Global Composite PMI came in at 58.4 in September
item.description: US business activity is predicted to have gained momentum in September, according to the flash reading of the S&P Global Composite PMI, which ticked up to 58.4 from 56.0 in August.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Bearish trend targets 1.4125 – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is marginally weaker versus the US Dollar (USD), with USD/CAD at its highest since late July. They stress wide yield spreads and typical negative Q4 seasonality as key headwinds for CAD.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens ahead of SNB rate decision
item.description: USD/CHF edges higher on Wednesday, snapping a four-day losing streak as the US Dollar (USD) continues to attract buying following the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) hawkish rate hike at its September 15-16 policy meeting.

item.title: British Pound: BoE repricing risk keeps Pound vulnerable – BBH
item.description: According to Elias Haddad at Brown Brothers Harriman, GBP/USD is lower on broad Dollar strength and EUR/GBP is slightly firmer after weaker United Kingdom (UK) September Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI).

item.title: Oil rebounds above $90: Why is the Canadian Dollar still falling?
item.description: USD/CAD extends its advance on Wednesday and trades around 1.4090 at the time of writing, up 0.21% on the day. The pair remains close to its recent highs, supported by a firm US Dollar (USD), while the Canadian Dollar (CAD) struggles to recover losses from the recent decline in Oil prices.

item.title: Euro: Downside bias toward 1.1400 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann keep a negative stance on EUR/USD after the pair closed at 1.1447. They see scope for further Euro (EUR) weakness, with intraday support at 1.1415 and a key level at 1.1400, though they doubt a sustained break lower.

item.title: Gold: Next leg higher toward $5,000 – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay argues Gold is entering a new bullish phase, with speculative, ETF and central bank flows reinforcing resilience despite further Fed hikes.

item.title: Copper: Chinese tightness supports prices despite weak positioning – ING
item.description: ING analysts Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson report that LME Copper has extended gains on tight physical conditions in China, falling inventories and holiday-related restocking, even as investor positioning remains subdued.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Daily range holds, but 4-hour chart turns bearish
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) slides nearly 3% on Wednesday as the hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook pushes the US Dollar (USD) to a two-month high and weighs on non-yielding metals. Gold (XAU/USD) is also down more than 1%. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $65.

item.title: US Dollar: Growth edge narrative supports gains – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the Dollar is extending gains as US economic data and policy dynamics remain supportive. September US PMI is expected to confirm US growth leadership versus Eurozone, UK and Japan.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Range-bound trading outlook against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see USD/CHF stuck in tight ranges across timeframes. Intraday, they expect the US Dollar (USD) to hold between 0.8185 and 0.8230 as prior downside momentum has faded.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Rally extend to near 101.00 as hawkish Fed narrative takes hold
item.description: The US Dollar trades higher as financial markets embrace hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) view. As of writing, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, trades 0.35% higher to near 100.90, the highest level seen in over seven weeks.

item.title: Euro rallies against a weak British Pound as UK business activity disappoints
item.description: The Euro (EUR) accelerates its recovery against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday as mixed UK Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) figures reveal that inflationary pressures have weighed heavily on business activity in September.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Growth and future rate outlook favour SEK – Societe Generale
item.description: Kit Juckes at Societe Generale argues that Swedish Krona (SEK) is poised to benefit from Sweden’s superior growth outlook and expected Riksbank tightening.

item.title: Oil: Prices retreat on Saudi exports and US data – ING
item.description: ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson note that Brent and WTI have sold off sharply as expectations of higher Saudi crude exports, progress in US-Iran talks and a surprise US inventory build ease Middle East supply concerns.

item.title: Indian Rupee resumes decline as markets embrace hawkish Fed view
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after rising in the past few trading days.

item.title: Silver price falls as Fed tightening bets, US-Iran talks curb safe-haven demand
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Wednesday, trading around $65.20 at the time of writing, down 2.80% on the day. The white metal retreats further from the $68.00 area as a stronger US Dollar (USD) and a hawkish repricing of the US interest rate outlook weigh on precious metals.

item.title: Japanese Yen exposes to two-week low against US Dollar, US PMI eyed
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to underperform against the US Dollar (USD), with the USD/JPY pair trading 0.3% higher to near 157.85 during the European session on Wednesday. The USD/JPY pair is little far from the two-week high of 158.05 posted on Friday.

item.title: British Pound tests 12-week lows amid mixed UK PMIs and US Dollar strength
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) accelerates its decline against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the GBP/USD pair trading a few pips above 1.3272, its lowest price since July 2.

item.title: Euro: PMI strength limits downside against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD is weaker on broad Dollar strength, but Eurozone data and European Central Bank (ECB) expectations cushion the downside. September Eurozone Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) beat forecasts, supporting additional ECB hikes.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD drifts toward $4.300 with bears gaining traction
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retraces Tuesday’s gains on Wednesday and drifts lower, approaching the $4,300 area as the US Dollar Index (DXY) rallies further amid high US Treasury yields.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Bearish outlook retained below 0.7140 - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann describe AUD/USD price action as range-bound around 0.7115, with intraday expectations for 0.7095–0.7125.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.45 per troy ounce, down 2.42% from the $67.07 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Staying strong as Fed expectations hold – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar’s resilience despite lower Oil prices and improved global risk sentiment, highlighting that hawkish Federal Reserve communication is keeping the Dollar supported.

item.title: British Pound holds steady against Japanese Yen after mixed UK PMIs
item.description: GBP/JPY trades around 209.90 on Wednesday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day with a modest 0.05% decline.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Cautious MNB stance supports HUF – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke reviews the Hungarian Central Bank decision to keep the key rate at 5.50% while lowering its medium-term inflation target to 2.5% from 2028. The MNB slightly raised its 2027 inflation forecast and will move to eight policy meetings per year.

item.title: Euro dips against Canadian Dollar following HCOB PMI data release
item.description: EUR/CAD halts its four day-winning streak, trading around 1.6090 during the European hours on Wednesday. The currency cross is under pressure as the Euro (EUR) holds losses following the release of the latest HCOB Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data for Germany and the broader Eurozone.

item.title: Euro remains depressed as German politics, France's debt offset strong PMI figures
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains on its back foot against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, extending its decline to two-and-a-half-month lows after dropping about 0.5% so far this week.
